hook: I paid online, but my **order never arrived.**
hook_q: My online order never arrived. What are my rights?

slides.title: Online buyers are **consumers too.**
slides.body: Buying online counts as buying goods under the Consumer Protection Act. The E-Commerce Rules cover all goods and services sold online, on marketplace and inventory platforms.
slides.ref: CPA 2019 · Sec 2(7) Expl (b) · E-Commerce Rules 2020 · Rule 2(1)

slides.title: Late delivery? **No refusing a refund.**
slides.body: A marketplace seller, or a platform selling its own stock, can't refuse to take back goods or refund what you paid if delivery is late from the stated schedule.
slides.note: except delays due to force majeure

timeline.text: Complain to the platform's grievance officer. Their **name and contact** must be shown on the platform.

slides.title: Get a **ticket number.**
slides.body: Marketplaces must give a ticket number for each complaint so you can track its status, and must show their return, refund, delivery and shipment information.

slides.title: Accepted refunds must **be paid.**
slides.body: Platforms must pay accepted refunds within a reasonable time, as prescribed by the RBI or any other competent authority, or as applicable law requires.

slides.title: No reply? **Call 1915.**
slides.body: The National Consumer Helpline handles grievances at the pre-litigation stage. Call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915. Platforms must try to partner with it.

slides.title: Last step: **Consumer Commission.**
slides.body: You can file a complaint over an unfair trade practice or a deficient service, including online on e-Jagriti.

sources: PIB: E-Commerce (Amendment) Rules 2026 (10 Sep 2026); NCH and e-Jagriti (2025–26)
caption:
Paid online but your order never came? Here's what the rules say. 👇

1️⃣ Online purchases are covered by the Consumer Protection Act and the E-Commerce Rules, 2020
2️⃣ A seller or platform can't refuse a refund if delivery is late from the stated schedule (except force majeure)
3️⃣ Complain to the platform's grievance officer: acknowledgement within 48 hours, redressal within 1 month
4️⃣ Marketplaces must give you a ticket number to track your complaint
5️⃣ No luck? Call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915
6️⃣ Still unresolved? File a consumer complaint, online on e-Jagriti

Source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 (Rules 2, 4, 5, 6, 7); Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Sec 2(6), 2(7)); PIB
